title: Automated Legacy System Refactoring
business: Enterprise software maintenance teams managing monolithic codebases.
problem: Manual refactoring of legacy modules often leads to regression errors and inconsistent architectural patterns due to the sheer scale of the codebase.
solution: GPT-5.1-Codex-Max provides a high-capacity agentic environment via the Responses API, allowing the model to maintain deep context across massive file structures to perform systematic, multi-step refactoring tasks.
steps: Initialize a session using the Responses API to establish a persistent context for the codebase.
Upload the legacy module architecture as structured input to leverage the 400,000 token context window.
Define refactoring rules using function calling to ensure the model adheres to modern design patterns.
Execute the refactoring process in stages, utilizing the model's reasoning capabilities to validate dependencies.
Review the generated output stream to verify compliance with the target architectural standards.
outcome: A more maintainable, modular codebase with reduced technical debt and improved consistency across legacy components.
limitation: The model's reliance on the Responses API means it is not compatible with standard Chat Completions workflows, requiring developers to re-architect their integration layer to handle asynchronous response streams.
